claims.evidence_en: It is already known from various publications that certain benzoylcyclohexanediones, among others also those which for example carry a radical linked through a bridge in the 3-position of the phenyl ring, possess herbicidal properties. Thus JP-A 08 020554 describes such benzoylcyclohexanediones which carry a substituted phenoxymethyl radical in the said position. JP-A 02 00222 describes benzoylcyclohexanediones which likewise carry a radical linked through a bridge in the said 3-position, [where] this bridge contains at least one atom from the group consisting of oxygen, sulfur and nitrogen. WO 99/10327, WO 99/07688 and WO 99/03845 describe benzoylcyclohexanediones which carry, in the 3-position, a heterocyclic radical linked through a carbon chain which, in the case of WO 99/07688, may also be interrupted by heteroatoms. However, the use in practice of the benzoylcyclohexanediones known from these publications is frequently attended by disadvantages. Thus the herbicidal or plant-growth-regulating activity of the known compounds is not always sufficient, or, where the herbicidal activity is sufficient, undesirable damage to the crop plants is observed.

claims.evidence_en: (54) Title: BENZOYLCYCLOHEXANEDIONES, PROCESS FOR THEIR PREPARATION AND THEIR USE AS HERBICIDES AND PLANT GROWTH REGULATORS (57) Abstract Benzoylcyclohexanediones of the general formula (I), processes for their preparation and their use as herbicides and plant growth regulators are described. In this general formula (I), R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6 and R7 stand for various radicals, L for an alkylene chain, Y and Z for a monoatomic bridging element. Benzoylcyclohexanediones, processes for their preparation, and their use as herbicides and plant growth regulators It is already known from various publications that certain benzoylcyclohexanediones, among others also those which for example carry a radical linked through a bridge in the 3-position of the phenyl ring, possess herbicidal properties. Thus JP-A 08 020554 describes such benzoylcyclohexanediones which carry a substituted phenoxymethyl radical in the said position. JP-A 02 00222 describes benzoylcyclohexanediones which likewise carry a radical linked through a bridge in the said 3-position, [where] this bridge contains at least one atom from the group consisting of oxygen, sulfur and nitrogen. WO 99/10327, WO 99/07688 and WO 99/03845 describe benzoylcyclohexanediones which carry, in the 3-position, a heterocyclic radical linked through a carbon chain which, in the case of WO 99/07688, may also be interrupted by heteroatoms. However, the use in practice of the benzoylcyclohexanediones known from these publications is frequently attended by disadvantages. Thus the herbicidal or plant-growth-regulating activity of the known compounds is not always sufficient, or, where the herbicidal activity is sufficient, undesirable damage to the crop plants is observed.

claims.evidence_en: Seeds of monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous weeds are laid out in cardboard pots in sandy loam soil, covered with earth and raised in the greenhouse under good growth conditions. Two to three weeks after sowing, the test plants are treated at the three-leaf stage. The compounds according to the invention, formulated as wettable powders or as emulsion concentrates, are sprayed onto the green parts of the plants at a dosage equivalent to 1 kg of active substance or less per hectare with a water application rate equivalent to 600 to 800 l/ha. After 3 to 4 weeks of standing time of the test plants in the greenhouse under optimal growth conditions, the effect of the preparations is assessed in comparison with untreated controls. The agents according to the invention also show good herbicidal activity in post-emergence against a broad spectrum of economically important grass weeds and broadleaf weeds. For example, the compounds of Examples Nos. 20, 32, 33, 34 and 18 show at least 80 % activity against Sinapis arvensis and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples Nos. 2, 20, 33 and 34 show at least 80 % activity against Stellaria media and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples Nos. 2 and 18 show at least 90 % activity against Sinapis arvensis and Stellaria media.

Likewise, stereoisomers can be prepared selectively by employing stereoselective reactions using optically active starting materials and/or auxiliaries. The invention also relates to all stereoisomers and mixtures thereof which are encompassed by the general formula I but are not specifically defined.

claims.evidence_en: On account of their herbicidal and plant growth regulating properties, the active substances can also be used for controlling harmful plants in crops of genetically modified plants which are known or still to be developed. The transgenic plants are as a rule distinguished by particular advantageous properties, for example by resistances to certain pesticides, above all certain herbicides, resistances to plant diseases or to pathogens of plant diseases such as certain insects or microorganisms such as fungi, bacteria or viruses. Other particular properties concern for example the  harvested product with regard to quantity, quality, storability, composition and specific constituents. Thus transgenic plants with increased starch content or altered quality of the starch, or such with a different fatty acid composition of the harvested product, are known. On application of the active substances according to the invention in transgenic crops, there occur, in addition to the effects against Furthermore, the substances according to the invention have outstanding growth-regulatory properties in crop plants. They intervene in a regulatory manner in the plant's own metabolism and can thus be used for the targeted influencing of plant constituents and for facilitating harvesting, such as for example by triggering desiccation and stunting of growth. The mixture was left to stir overnight at room temperature and was then concentrated under high vacuum on a rotary evaporator. The residue was dissolved in 16 ml of tetrahydrofuran and 8 ml of water and boiled under reflux for 4 h together with 0.23 g of NaOH (5.85 mmol). It was then allowed to cool, largely concentrated on a rotary evaporator and the aqueous residue was then treated with 2 M HCl. It was then extracted with methylene chloride, the combined organic phase was dried over MgSO4 and evaporated to dryness on a rotary evaporator.
Yield:	0.67 g (67 % of theory), colourless oil

0.67 g (1.97 mmol) of 2-chloro-4-methylsulfonyl-3-phenoxymethyl-benzoic acid in 30 ml of methylene chloride were treated with 2 drops of N,N-dimethylformamide and 0.76 g (5.9 mmol) of oxalyl chloride and boiled under reflux for 2.5 h. It was then stripped off on the rotary evaporator, the residue was taken up in 30 ml of methylene chloride and treated at 0 °C with 0.24 g (2.16 mmol) of cyclohexanedione and 0.60 g (5.9 mmol) of triethylamine. It was left to stir on for 4 h at room temperature. It was then concentrated on the rotary evaporator and purified chromatographically (silica gel, ethyl acetate:hexane = 1:1).

claims.evidence_en: Seeds of monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous weeds are laid out in cardboard pots in sandy loam soil, covered with earth and raised in the greenhouse under good growth conditions. Two to three weeks after sowing, the test plants are treated at the three-leaf stage. The compounds according to the invention, formulated as wettable powders or as emulsion concentrates, are sprayed onto the green parts of the plants at a dosage equivalent to 1 kg of active substance or less per hectare with a water application rate equivalent to 600 to 800 l/ha. After 3 to 4 weeks of standing time of the test plants in the greenhouse under optimal growth conditions, the effect of the preparations is assessed in comparison with untreated controls. The agents according to the invention also show good herbicidal activity in post-emergence against a broad spectrum of economically important grass weeds and broadleaf weeds. For example, the compounds of Examples Nos. 20, 32, 33, 34 and 18 show at least 80 % activity against Sinapis arvensis and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples Nos. 2, 20, 33 and 34 show at least 80 % activity against Stellaria media and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples Nos. 2 and 18 show at least 90 % activity against Sinapis arvensis and Stellaria media.

claims.evidence_en: Seeds of monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous weeds are laid out in cardboard pots in sandy loam soil, covered with earth and raised in the greenhouse under good growth conditions. Two to three weeks after sowing, the test plants are treated at the three-leaf stage. The compounds according to the invention, formulated as wettable powders or as emulsion concentrates, are sprayed onto the green parts of the plants at a dosage equivalent to 1 kg of active substance or less per hectare with a water application rate equivalent to 600 to 800 l/ha. After 3 to 4 weeks of standing time of the test plants in the greenhouse under optimal growth conditions, the effect of the preparations is assessed in comparison with untreated controls. The agents according to the invention also show good herbicidal activity in post-emergence against a broad spectrum of economically important grass weeds and broadleaf weeds. For example, the compounds of Examples Nos. 20, 32, 33, 34 and 18 show at least 80 % activity against Sinapis arvensis and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples Nos. 2, 20, 33 and 34 show at least 80 % activity against Stellaria media and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples Nos. 2 and 18 show at least 90 % activity against Sinapis arvensis and Stellaria media.

claims.evidence_en: In further trials in the greenhouse, seeds of a relatively large number of crop plants and weeds are laid out in sandy loam soil and covered with soil. Some of the pots are treated immediately as described under section 1, the remainder are placed in the greenhouse until the plants have developed two to three true leaves and are then sprayed as described under section 2 with the substances of the formula (I) according to the invention at different dosages. Four to five weeks after the application and after standing in the greenhouse, it is established by visual assessment that the compounds according to the invention as a rule leave dicotyledonous crops such as, for example, soybean and sugar beet undamaged or almost undamaged in the pre- and post-emergence method, even at high active-substance dosages. Some substances additionally spare graminaceous crops such as, for example, barley, wheat and rice. The compounds of the formula (I) show in part a high selectivity and are therefore suitable for controlling undesired plant growth in agricultural crops.

claims.evidence_en: (54) Title: BENZOYLCYCLOHEXANEDIONES, PROCESS FOR THEIR PREPARATION AND THEIR USE AS HERBICIDES AND PLANT GROWTH REGULATORS (57) Abstract Benzoylcyclohexanediones of the general formula (I), processes for their preparation and their use as herbicides and plant growth regulators are described. In this general formula (I), R1, R2, R3, R4, R5, R6 and R7 stand for various radicals, L for an alkylene chain, Y and Z for a monoatomic bridging element. Benzoylcyclohexanediones, processes for their preparation, and their use as herbicides and plant growth regulators It is already known from various publications that certain benzoylcyclohexanediones, among others also those which for example carry a radical linked through a bridge in the 3-position of the phenyl ring, possess herbicidal properties. Thus JP-A 08 020554 describes such benzoylcyclohexanediones which carry a substituted phenoxymethyl radical in the said position. JP-A 02 00222 describes benzoylcyclohexanediones which likewise carry a radical linked through a bridge in the said 3-position, [where] this bridge contains at least one atom from the group consisting of oxygen, sulfur and nitrogen. WO 99/10327, WO 99/07688 and WO 99/03845 describe benzoylcyclohexanediones which carry, in the 3-position, a heterocyclic radical linked through a carbon chain which, in the case of WO 99/07688, may also be interrupted by heteroatoms. However, the use in practice of the benzoylcyclohexanediones known from these publications is frequently attended by disadvantages. Thus the herbicidal or plant-growth-regulating activity of the known compounds is not always sufficient, or, where the herbicidal activity is sufficient, undesirable damage to the crop plants is observed.

If, for example, one or more alkenyl groups are present, diastereomers may occur. If, for example, one or more asymmetric carbon atoms are present, enantiomers and diastereomers may occur. Stereoisomers can be obtained from the mixtures arising in the preparation by customary separation methods, for example by chromatographic separation processes. Likewise, stereoisomers can be prepared selectively by employing stereoselective reactions using optically active starting materials and/or auxiliaries. The invention also relates to all stereoisomers and mixtures thereof which are encompassed by the general formula I but are not specifically defined.

In this it is generally immaterial whether the substances are applied by the pre-sowing, pre-emergence or post-emergence method. In detail, some representatives of the monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous weed flora that are controlled by the compounds according to the invention may be named by way of example Harmful plants occurring under the specific cultivation conditions in rice, such as, for example, Echinochloa, Sagittaria, Alisma, Eleocharis, Scirpus and Cyperus, are likewise outstandingly controlled by the active compounds according to the invention. On application of the active compounds to the green parts of the plants by the post-emergence method, growth likewise stops drastically very soon after the treatment, and the weed plants remain at the growth stage present at the time of application, or die completely after a certain time, so that in this way weed competition harmful to the crop plants is eliminated very early and lastingly. On account of their herbicidal and plant growth regulating properties, the active substances can also be used for controlling harmful plants in crops of genetically modified plants which are known or still to be developed. The transgenic plants are as a rule distinguished by particular advantageous properties, for example by resistances to certain pesticides, above all certain herbicides, resistances to plant diseases or to pathogens of plant diseases such as certain insects or microorganisms such as fungi, bacteria or viruses. Other particular properties concern for example the  harvested product with regard to quantity, quality, storability, composition and specific constituents. Thus transgenic plants with increased starch content or altered quality of the starch, or such with a different fatty acid composition of the harvested product, are known. They intervene in a regulatory manner in the plant's own metabolism and can thus be used for the targeted influencing of plant constituents and for facilitating harvesting, such as for example by triggering desiccation and stunting of growth. Moreover, they are also suitable for the general control and inhibition of unwanted vegetative growth without killing the plants in the process. An inhibition of vegetative growth plays a major role in many monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous crops, since lodging can thereby be reduced or completely prevented.

claims.evidence_en: The compounds of the formula (I) according to the invention exhibit excellent herbicidal activity against a broad spectrum of economically important monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous harmful plants. Perennial weeds that are difficult to control and that shoot from rhizomes, rootstocks or other perennating organs are also well controlled by the active ingredients. In this it is generally immaterial whether the substances are applied by the pre-sowing, pre-emergence or post-emergence method. In detail, some representatives of the monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous weed flora that are controlled by the compounds according to the invention may be named by way of example If the compounds according to the invention are applied to the soil surface before germination, then either the emergence of the weed seedlings is completely prevented, or the weeds grow until they reach the cotyledon stage but then stop growing and, after a period of three to four weeks has elapsed, finally die completely. Although the compounds according to the invention have excellent herbicidal activity against monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous weeds, crop plants of economically important crops such as, for example, wheat, barley, rye, rice, maize, sugar beet, cotton and soya are damaged only insignificantly, or not at all. For these reasons, the present compounds are very well suited for the selective control of undesired plant growth in agricultural crop plantings or in ornamental plantings. Preferred is the use of the compounds of the formula (I) according to the invention, or their salts, in economically important transgenic crops of useful and ornamental plants, for example of cereals such as wheat, barley, rye, oats, millet, rice, cassava and maize, or also crops of sugar beet, cotton, soya, oilseed rape, potato, tomato, pea and other kinds of vegetable. Preferably the compounds of the formula (I) can be used as herbicides in crops of useful plants which are resistant to the phytotoxic effects of the herbicides, or have been made resistant by genetic engineering. The compounds according to the invention can preferably be used in transgenic crops which are resistant to herbicides from the group of the sulfonylureas, glufosinate-ammonium or glyphosate-isopropylammonium and analogous active substances. The invention therefore also relates to the use of the compounds according to the invention as herbicides for controlling damaging plants in transgenic crop plants. The compounds according to the invention can be applied in the form of wettable powders, emulsifiable concentrates, sprayable solutions, dusts or granules in the customary preparations. The invention therefore also relates to herbicidal and plant-growth-regulating compositions which contain compounds of the formula (I). The compounds of the formula (I) can be formulated in various ways, depending on which biological and/or chemical-physical parameters are prescribed. Possible formulations are for example: wettable powders (WP), water-soluble powders (SP), water-soluble concentrates, emulsifiable concentrates (EC), emulsions (EW), such as oil-in-water and water- The agrochemical preparations generally contain 0.1 to 99% by weight, in particular 0.1 to 95% by weight, of active ingredient of the formula (I). As combination partners for the active compounds according to the invention in mixture formulations or in a tank mix, known active compounds can be used, for example those described in Weed Research 26, 441-445 (1986) or "The Pesticide Manual", 11th edition, The British Crop Protection Council and the Royal Soc. of Chemistry, 1997 and in the literature cited therein. Known herbicides which can be combined with the compounds of the formula (I) include, for example, the following active compounds (note: the compounds are designated either by the "common name" according to the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) or by the chemical name, where appropriate together with a customary code number): The application rate of the compounds of the formula (I) required varies with the external conditions such as temperature, humidity, the nature of the herbicide used, among others. It can vary within wide limits, for example between 0.001 and 10.0 kg/ha or more of active substance, but preferably it lies between 0.005 and 5 kg/ha. In further trials in the greenhouse, seeds of a relatively large number of crop plants and weeds are laid out in sandy loam soil and covered with soil. Some of the pots are treated immediately as described under section 1, the remainder are placed in the greenhouse until the plants have developed two to three true leaves and are then sprayed as described under section 2 with the substances of the formula (I) according to the invention at different dosages. Four to five weeks after the application and after standing in the greenhouse, it is established by visual assessment that the compounds according to the invention as a rule leave dicotyledonous crops such as, for example, soybean and sugar beet undamaged or almost undamaged in the pre- and post-emergence method, even at high active-substance dosages. Some substances additionally spare graminaceous crops such as, for example, barley, wheat and rice. The compounds of the formula (I) show in part a high selectivity and are therefore suitable for controlling undesired plant growth in agricultural crops. The claims 1-12 as they stand relate to a disproportionately large number of possible compounds, of which only a small proportion can be regarded as supported by the description within the meaning of Art. 6 PCT and/or as disclosed in the application within the meaning of Art. 5 PCT. In the present case the claims lack the corresponding support and the application lacks the necessary disclosure to such an extent that a meaningful search over the whole of the claimed scope appears impossible. The search was therefore directed to those parts of the claims which appear supported and disclosed in the above sense, namely to the parts concerning the compounds of formula (I) with R1 equal to O-hydrocarbyl residue or S-hydrocarbyl residue; R2 = halogen; R3 = S(O)2-alkyl; R4 = R5 = H; R7 = H or methyl; R6 = OH or O-protecting group and L = C1-C6 alkylene chain.

claims.evidence_en: Seeds of monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous weed plants are laid out in cardboard pots in sandy loam soil and covered with soil. The compounds according to the invention, formulated as wettable powders or emulsion concentrates, are then applied to the surface of the covering soil as an aqueous suspension or emulsion at a water application rate equivalent to 600 to 800 l/ha, at a dosage equivalent to 1 kg of active substance or less per hectare. After the treatment the pots are placed in the greenhouse and kept under good growth conditions for the weeds. The visual assessment of damage to the plants and of emergence damage is carried out after emergence of the test plants, following a test period of 3 to 4 weeks, by comparison with untreated controls. Here, for example, the compounds of Examples No. 5, 33 and 19 show an action of at least 80 % against Stellaria media, Lolium multiflorum and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples No. 2 and 8 show an action of at least 90 % against Amaranthus retroflexus, Stellaria media and Setaria viridis. The compounds of Examples No. 2 and 18 show a 100 % action against Amaranthus retroflexus and Sinapis arvensis. Seeds of monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous weeds are laid out in cardboard pots in sandy loam soil, covered with earth and raised in the greenhouse under good growth conditions. Two to three weeks after sowing, the test plants are treated at the three-leaf stage. The compounds according to the invention, formulated as wettable powders or as emulsion concentrates, are sprayed onto the green parts of the plants at a dosage equivalent to 1 kg of active substance or less per hectare with a water application rate equivalent to 600 to 800 l/ha. After 3 to 4 weeks of standing time of the test plants in the greenhouse under optimal growth conditions, the effect of the preparations is assessed in comparison with untreated controls. The agents according to the invention also show good herbicidal activity in post-emergence against a broad spectrum of economically important grass weeds and broadleaf weeds. For example, the compounds of Examples Nos. 20, 32, 33, 34 and 18 show at least 80 % activity against Sinapis arvensis and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples Nos. 2, 20, 33 and 34 show at least 80 % activity against Stellaria media and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples Nos. 2 and 18 show at least 90 % activity against Sinapis arvensis and Stellaria media.

After the treatment the pots are placed in the greenhouse and kept under good growth conditions for the weeds. The visual assessment of damage to the plants and of emergence damage is carried out after emergence of the test plants, following a test period of 3 to 4 weeks, by comparison with untreated controls. Here, for example, the compounds of Examples No. 5, 33 and 19 show an action of at least 80 % against Stellaria media, Lolium multiflorum and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples No. 2 and 8 show an action of at least 90 % against Amaranthus retroflexus, Stellaria media and Setaria viridis. The compounds of Examples No. 2 and 18 show a 100 % action against Amaranthus retroflexus and Sinapis arvensis. Typical harmful plants in rice cultures are raised in the greenhouse under paddy rice conditions (water impoundment height: 2 – 3 cm). After treatment with the formulated compounds according to the invention at a dosage equivalent to 1 kg of active substance or less per hectare, the test plants are placed in the greenhouse under optimal growth conditions and kept so for the whole duration of the trial. About three weeks after the application, the evaluation is carried out by visual assessment of the plant damage in comparison with untreated controls. The compounds according to the invention show very good herbicidal activity against harmful plants. For example, the compounds of Examples Nos.

claims.evidence_en: Seeds of monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous weeds are laid out in cardboard pots in sandy loam soil, covered with earth and raised in the greenhouse under good growth conditions. Two to three weeks after sowing, the test plants are treated at the three-leaf stage. The compounds according to the invention, formulated as wettable powders or as emulsion concentrates, are sprayed onto the green parts of the plants at a dosage equivalent to 1 kg of active substance or less per hectare with a water application rate equivalent to 600 to 800 l/ha. After 3 to 4 weeks of standing time of the test plants in the greenhouse under optimal growth conditions, the effect of the preparations is assessed in comparison with untreated controls. The agents according to the invention also show good herbicidal activity in post-emergence against a broad spectrum of economically important grass weeds and broadleaf weeds. For example, the compounds of Examples Nos. 20, 32, 33, 34 and 18 show at least 80 % activity against Sinapis arvensis and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples Nos. 2, 20, 33 and 34 show at least 80 % activity against Stellaria media and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples Nos. 2 and 18 show at least 90 % activity against Sinapis arvensis and Stellaria media.

claims.evidence_en: Claims Nos. 1-12  relate to a disproportionately large number of possible compounds, products and methods of which only a small proportion are supported by the description according to the terms of Article 6 PCT and/or can be considered disclosed according to the terms of Article 5 PCT. In the present case, the patent claims lack the appropriate support and the patent application lacks the required disclosure to such an extent that a meaningful search encompassing the entire scope of protection sought seems impossible.For this reason the search was directed at parts of the claims that seemed to be supported and disclosed according to the above mentioned terms, i.e. parts relating to compounds of formula (I), wherein R1 is equal to an O-hydrocarbon radical or S-hydrocarbon radical ; R2 = halogen, R3 = S(O)2-alkyl ; R4 = R5 = H ; R7 = H or methyl ; R6 = OH or an O-protective group and L= C1-C6 alkylene chain.

Benzoylcyclohexanediones, processes for their preparation, and their use as herbicides and plant growth regulators
Benzoylcyclohexanediones, processes for their preparation, and their use as herbicides and plant growth regulators

The invention relates to the technical field of herbicides and plant growth regulators, in particular that of herbicides for the selective control of broad-leaved weeds and grass weeds in crops of useful plants.

The invention relates to the technical field of herbicides and plant growth regulators, in particular that of herbicides for the selective control of broad-leaved weeds and grass weeds in crops of useful plants.

It is already known from various publications that certain benzoylcyclohexanediones, among others also those which for example carry a radical linked through a bridge in the 3-position of the phenyl ring, possess herbicidal properties. Thus JP-A 08 020554 describes such benzoylcyclohexanediones which carry a substituted phenoxymethyl radical in the said position. JP-A 02 00222 describes benzoylcyclohexanediones which likewise carry a radical linked through a bridge in the said 3-position, [where] this bridge contains at least one atom from the group consisting of oxygen, sulfur and nitrogen. WO 99/10327, WO 99/07688 and WO 99/03845 describe benzoylcyclohexanediones which carry, in the 3-position, a heterocyclic radical linked through a carbon chain which, in the case of WO 99/07688, may also be interrupted by heteroatoms.

However, the use in practice of the benzoylcyclohexanediones known from these publications is frequently attended by disadvantages. Thus the herbicidal or plant-growth-regulating activity of the known compounds is not always sufficient, or, where the herbicidal activity is sufficient, undesirable damage to the crop plants is observed.

A hydrocarbon radical is a straight-chain, branched or cyclic, saturated, partially saturated, unsaturated or aromatic radical, e.g. alkyl, alkenyl, alkynyl, cycloalkyl, cycloalkenyl, cycloalkynyl or aryl. Composite terms such as cycloalkylalkenyl, cycloalkynylalkyl and arylalkynyl are likewise intended to be covered by this definition. If this hydrocarbon radical additionally contains heteroatoms, these can in principle, that is to say in so far as the chemical structure permits, be located at any position of the hydrocarbon radical. By definition, a heteroatom can also act as the linking atom to the rest of the molecule. A heteroatom can be singly or doubly bonded.

lines.text_en: Depending on the nature and linkage of the substituents, the compounds of the general formula I may be present as stereoisomers. If, for example, one or more alkenyl groups are present, diastereomers may occur. If, for example, one or more asymmetric carbon atoms are present, enantiomers and diastereomers may occur. Stereoisomers can be obtained from the mixtures arising in the preparation by customary separation methods, for example by chromatographic separation processes. Likewise, stereoisomers can be prepared selectively by employing stereoselective reactions using optically active starting materials and/or auxiliaries. The invention also relates to all stereoisomers and mixtures thereof which are encompassed by the general formula I but are not specifically defined.

1.    Herbicidal action on weeds, pre-emergence
1.    Herbicidal action on weeds, pre-emergence

Seeds of monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous weed plants are laid out in cardboard pots in sandy loam soil and covered with soil. The compounds according to the invention, formulated as wettable powders or emulsion concentrates, are then applied to the surface of the covering soil as an aqueous suspension or emulsion at a water application rate equivalent to 600 to 800 l/ha, at a dosage equivalent to 1 kg of active substance or less per hectare. After the treatment the pots are placed in the greenhouse and kept under good growth conditions for the weeds. The visual assessment of damage to the plants and of emergence damage is carried out after emergence of the test plants, following a test period of 3 to 4 weeks, by comparison with untreated controls. Here, for example, the compounds of Examples No. 5, 33 and 19 show an action of at least 80 % against Stellaria media, Lolium multiflorum and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples No. 2 and 8 show an action of at least 90 % against Amaranthus retroflexus, Stellaria media and Setaria viridis. The compounds of Examples No. 2 and 18 show a 100 % action against Amaranthus retroflexus and Sinapis arvensis.

2.	Weed control in post-emergence
2.	Weed control in post-emergence

Seeds of monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous weeds are laid out in cardboard pots in sandy loam soil, covered with earth and raised in the greenhouse under good growth conditions. Two to three weeks after sowing, the test plants are treated at the three-leaf stage. The compounds according to the invention, formulated as wettable powders or as emulsion concentrates, are sprayed onto the green parts of the plants at a dosage equivalent to 1 kg of active substance or less per hectare with a water application rate equivalent to 600 to 800 l/ha. After 3 to 4 weeks of standing time of the test plants in the greenhouse under optimal growth conditions, the effect of the preparations is assessed in comparison with untreated controls. The agents according to the invention also show good herbicidal activity in post-emergence against a broad spectrum of economically important grass weeds and broadleaf weeds. For example, the compounds of Examples Nos. 20, 32, 33, 34 and 18 show at least 80 % activity against Sinapis arvensis and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples Nos. 2, 20, 33 and 34 show at least 80 % activity against Stellaria media and Amaranthus retroflexus. The compounds of Examples Nos. 2 and 18 show at least 90 % activity against Sinapis arvensis and Stellaria media.

4.	Crop plant tolerance
4.	Crop plant tolerance

In further trials in the greenhouse, seeds of a relatively large number of crop plants and weeds are laid out in sandy loam soil and covered with soil. Some of the pots are treated immediately as described under section 1, the remainder are placed in the greenhouse until the plants have developed two to three true leaves and are then sprayed as described under section 2 with the substances of the formula (I) according to the invention at different dosages. Four to five weeks after the application and after standing in the greenhouse, it is established by visual assessment that the compounds according to the invention as a rule leave dicotyledonous crops such as, for example, soybean and sugar beet undamaged or almost undamaged in the pre- and post-emergence method, even at high active-substance dosages. Some substances additionally spare graminaceous crops such as, for example, barley, wheat and rice. The compounds of the formula (I) show in part a high selectivity and are therefore suitable for controlling undesired plant growth in agricultural crops.
